instruction: Using the given PDF template and employee data from the Excel sheet, fill out and generate an individual evaluation form for every employee. Use their full names for the PDF filenames and place all completed files on the Desktop, marking ratings with '√'.

metadata.explanation: This task verifies PDF file creation with comprehensive content validation for performance review forms. Verified employee names from Excel rows 2-5: 'John Doe', 'Emily Johnson', 'Michael Brown', 'Linda Green'. The evaluator checks that these 4 employees have PDFs with correct naming AND valid performance review content. Scoring: 0.25 points per file for existence + 0.25 points for substantial content (>200 chars with employee name) + 0.25 points for rating marks ('√') + 0.25 points for evaluation keywords (performance/rating/review/department/position/score), ensuring PDFs contain properly filled evaluation forms with actual review data.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.25 points per file for existence + 0.25 points for substantial content (>200 chars with employee name) + 0.25 points for rating marks ('√') + 0.25 points for evaluation keywords (4 files total)

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator provides comprehensive multi-dimensional verification of PDF performance review task
✅ Correctly verifies PDF file existence with exact employee names (John Doe.pdf, Emily Johnson.pdf, etc.)
✅ Validates substantial content (>200 chars) to prevent minimal/empty PDFs from passing
✅ Checks employee name appears in PDF content to ensure correct file-to-employee mapping
✅ Validates presence of '√' rating marks as specified in instruction (pdf.py:122-124)
✅ Checks for evaluation keywords (performance/rating/review/department/position/score) with threshold of 3+ keywords to ensure PDFs contain performance review content (pdf.py:127-134)
✅ Proportional scoring (0.25 per dimension × 4 dimensions) incentivizes completing all aspects of the task
✅ Getter logic correctly extracts PDF text using pdftotext and performs semantic validation
✅ Metric correctly handles 'expected' parameter when type='rule' (receives rules dict directly, accesses 'required_files' correctly)
✅ Expected values semantically correct (4 employee names verified from Excel data)
⚠️ Cannot verify if the provided template was actually used vs creating PDFs from scratch
⚠️ Cannot verify exact data transfer from Excel (e.g., specific ratings, departments, positions, scores from spreadsheet)
⚠️ Cannot verify form structure/fields match the template format
The evaluator uses semantic heuristics (rating marks, keywords, content length, name presence) to reasonably infer that PDFs contain properly filled evaluation forms rather than just minimal text
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: To achieve perfect verification (score 1.0), could add checks for specific Excel data fields (e.g., verify department/position values from spreadsheet appear in corresponding PDFs)
Could validate template structure if template fields/patterns are known (though this adds complexity)
Current approach is pragmatic: uses multiple semantic indicators to verify task completion without requiring exact template matching
